artists.biography:
Dubstar are an English band, performing mostly dream pop and indie dance music, as well as occasional pop ballads and, on later releases, guitar-heavy rock with an industrial influence. The group was formed in 1992 by Steve Hillier and Chris Wilkie in Newcastle-upon-Tyne. Sarah Blackwood joined in 1993, replacing Hillier on vocals.

"Stars", the best-selling single by Dubstar, received a wide variety of play time in clubs. Many remixes were also created of this song and it was covered by metal band Lacuna Coil on their 2000 EP Halflife. "Stars" allowed Dubstar to achieve American recognition.

perplexity.description:
Two is the fifth studio album by English electronic pop band Dubstar, released on 6 May 2022 through their own label, Northern Writes. It follows their 2018 album One and marks the second album since the reunion of core members Sarah Blackwood and Chris Wilkie. Musically, Two continues Dubstar’s blend of electronic and pop styles, characterized by melodic synth arrangements, polished production, and Blackwood’s distinctive vocals, maintaining the indie-pop sensibility that defined their earlier work while incorporating contemporary electronic textures.

In the context of Dubstar’s discography, Two represents a mature phase of the band’s evolution, arriving more than two decades after their initial success in the 1990s. It re-established their presence on the UK Albums Chart, reaching number 86, their first chart entry since 1997’s Goodbye. Critical reception noted the album’s cohesive sound and the duo’s ability to balance nostalgic elements with modern production, appealing to both longtime fans and new listeners. Released independently, Two underscores Dubstar’s continued creative control and commitment to their signature electronic-pop fusion.
